Absolutely disgusting customer service.

The RUDE cashier should not be representing this business.

During my visit, she repeatedly talked about customers in Spanish, apparently assuming no one around her could understand what she was saying. She was wrong.

Apparently these customers left a few items near the appliances instead of being returned to the $4 bins, management simply asked them that it be put back. It was immediately returned. That should have ended the situation.

Instead, while those customers were still standing there paying for their purchases, this cashier continued insulting them in Spanish, repeatedly calling them “cochinos” and “puercos” (pigs), referring to them as slobs, and discussing them with other customers waiting in line. Publicly humiliating paying customers while they are still standing at the register is completely unacceptable.

The irony is unbelievable. The store itself was cluttered, disorganized, with opened boxes, merchandise scattered throughout the aisles, and messy floors. Yet this employee felt justified degrading customers over where a few items had been left.

Customers don’t always know where an unwanted item belongs, especially in a store that isn’t well organized. A professional employee simply returns the item to its proper place. They do not ridicule customers, insult them, or make them the subject of conversation for everyone else in line.

What was just as disappointing was management’s response. Management was aware of what was happening and chose not to intervene. By allowing this behavior to continue, they sent the message that publicly humiliating customers is acceptable in this store.

This experience was embarrassing, disrespectful, and completely unnecessary. No customer should ever have to stand at the register feeling humiliated while employees openly mock them.

If the owner truly values customer service and the reputation of this business, I sincerely hope this review is taken seriously. An employee who publicly insults paying customers and embarrasses them in front of others has no place representing your business.

I will gladly spend my money elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
Dear Albertsons Corporate,

First, I’d like to congratulate whoever championed the digital coupon program. It has accomplished something I didn’t think was possible—it has turned buying groceries into an interactive team-building exercise.

Mission accomplished.

Here’s how my Monday evening unfolded.

I worked a 10-hour day. I rushed home to make sure my children had picked up the house before guests arrived. Once that was handled, I headed to Albertsons because, unlike the smaller grocery store less than a mile from my house, Albertsons carries the Coke and ice cream cake my son wanted.

So far, so good.

I grabbed my items and noticed a promotion:

Buy 2 for $10.99. Get 2 Free.

Excellent.

I waited in line. And waited.

Every register was moving slower than expected, but I wasn’t paying much attention. I assumed it was just another busy Monday.

Finally, I reached the cashier and asked about the promotion.

“Oh…that’s a digital coupon.”

I’m sorry…what?

Apparently, the sale wasn’t actually a sale.

It was an invitation.

An invitation to download an app, create or sign into an account, find the coupon, “clip” it, and complete a small digital scavenger hunt while standing at the register with a line of people behind me.

Because nothing says “efficient checkout” quite like asking customers to complete IT onboarding while buying milk.

Here’s the irony.

I don’t mind waiting.

What I do mind is becoming the reason everyone else has to wait.

You know who else didn’t seem thrilled with this process?

Your employees.

As I stood there deciding whether I wanted groceries or a software installation, I started paying attention.

Customers at self-checkout were confused.

Other shoppers were asking why the sale wasn’t coming up.

Employees were repeatedly explaining the digital coupon process.

That’s when it hit me.

The reason every checkout lane felt unusually slow wasn’t because your employees were inefficient.

It was because Corporate had successfully inserted an extra step into every transaction.

That’s actually impressive.

You’ve managed to create a system that frustrates customers, slows checkout, increases employee workload, creates bottlenecks, and leaves everyone just a little more irritated than when they walked in.

That’s not innovation.

That’s operational gridlock with branding.

Technology should remove friction, not manufacture it.

If I’m already entering my phone number at checkout, why isn’t every eligible promotion automatically applied?

Why advertise a price that requires a separate digital obstacle course to receive?

If I have to stand at the register downloading an app just to buy cereal on sale, we’ve officially lost the plot.

In the end, I returned my entire purchase.

Not because I couldn’t figure out the app.

Because I shouldn’t have to.

Customers shouldn’t need a smartphone tutorial to buy groceries.

Your employees shouldn’t have to apologize for a corporate decision they didn’t make.

And checkout shouldn’t feel like I’m applying for TSA PreCheck.

The best customer experiences are the ones customers don’t have to think about.

When buying groceries starts requiring instructions, something has gone terribly wrong.

When was the last time the decision-makers who approved this digital coupon strategy actually went grocery shopping?

I mean alone. Tired. After a long day at work.

Not wanting to pull out a phone.
Not wanting to download an app.
Not wanting to scan a QR code.
Not wanting a tutorial in the checkout line.
Just wanting to buy groceries and go.

Because if the people making these decisions experienced their own checkout process, I have a hard time believing this policy would have survived the first meeting.

Respectfully,

Maria Cecilia Garcia

P.S. One last thought: if multiple customers are discovering they need an app only after waiting in line, that’s not a customer problem. That’s a process problem. And process problems are usually solved in conference rooms—not checkout lanes.

Do better!

Buying groceries should not require a smartphone, an app, and a QR code. 🙄

Unfortunately, my three experiences here have been consistently disappointing. The food quality does not justify the prices, the drinks have tasted weak and watered down, and the customer service from both the servers and host staff has been underwhelming.

I was also surprised to see a 1.5% charge labeled “State Land/River Usage Fee” added to the bill. While restaurants may charge mandatory fees when properly disclosed, the wording makes this sound like a government-imposed fee. Customers should ask what this fee actually represents and who imposes it. If it is simply a restaurant surcharge, it should be clearly identified as such.

Between the mediocre food, disappointing drinks, poor customer service, and additional fees, the overall experience simply isn't worth the price. The location is great, but the quality and service need to match what customers are being charged.
Group size
3-4 people, 5-8 people

My friends and I had been to this restaurant once before and had a nice experience. For that reason, we decided to celebrate my friend’s birthday there last night.

The experience was completely the opposite of what we had before. It started with the wings, which arrived cold. A couple of items were ordered but never came.

They were having an event at 8:00 p.m. We were still eating dessert and fries when a staff member came over and told us they were taking our table away and that we either had to buy tickets for the event or leave. We were rushed out and weren’t even given time to ask for our fries to be boxed up.

There were empty tables on the patio outside, but instead of moving us there, they simply cleared our table and took all of our leftovers.

Our party of six was no longer having fun at that point. We felt more like an inconvenience than valued customers. Yes, we didn’t buy tickets, but was it fair to be asked to leave during a birthday dinner? We didn’t even care for the country music. We just wanted to enjoy a nice dinner and celebrate my friend’s birthday.

I feel like the restaurant should plan events better and move diners to the patio if they need the indoor tables for an event. We were paying customers, too. Overall, it was an awful experience, with rude staff. My friends and I will not be back.

one_star_reviews.text:
★☆☆☆☆

I had a very disappointing and unprofessional experience at this Xfinity Branded Partner location.

During my first visit, the male employee helping me was wearing braces, and it was extremely difficult to understand what he was saying. Since English is not my first language, communication was especially challenging. A woman I know who was also at the store told me she had already been waiting for approximately four and a half hours without receiving meaningful assistance.

The next day, I purchased regular residential Xfinity Internet for approximately $40 per month with AutoPay at the Truxel Road corporate store. This was not a $30 prepaid plan.

After returning home, I discovered that my house did not have a usable coaxial outlet, so I returned to the Walerga Road location because it is only about six minutes from my home. I simply needed help scheduling an Xfinity technician.

Before the first male employee (the one with braces) even asked what plan I had purchased or checked my account, he immediately assumed that I had purchased a $30 prepaid plan. He told me that because it was supposedly prepaid, I needed to call a customer-service hotline myself and wait on the phone for two or three hours.

His tone was dismissive and condescending, almost as though I owed him something rather than being a new Xfinity customer asking for help. He did not ask any questions, verify my plan, or make any effort to understand the situation. From the beginning, it appeared that he had already decided not to help me.

After I explained that I had purchased regular residential Internet with AutoPay, he then gave me another reason for refusing assistance. He said they could not schedule a technician because I had purchased the service at another Xfinity location.

The entire situation made it feel as though the Walerga Road store and the Truxel Road store were two separate competing companies. I was not asking another internet provider for assistance. Both locations operate under the Xfinity name, and I was simply asking one Xfinity location to schedule an Xfinity technician for an active Xfinity account.

I then spoke with a Russian-speaking male employee named Mark. Mark initially began assisting me normally, and everything appeared to be going well.

However, another male employee with long black hair called Mark into the back room. After Mark returned, he spent approximately five seconds at the computer and suddenly told me that he could no longer help me.

I asked Mark to show me exactly what he was doing on the computer. Instead of opening an account tool, entering information, checking an error message, or genuinely attempting to schedule a technician, he simply clicked on an empty area of the screen and claimed that nothing could be done.

I have an educational background in programming, but you do not need to be a programmer to recognize that no meaningful action was being taken.

Is it Xfinity policy to refuse assistance because the customer opened the account at another Xfinity location? Why did Mark initially begin helping me but suddenly refuse after being called into the back room?

The employees appeared more concerned about which store had sold the service than about helping an Xfinity customer. This experience was misleading, dismissive, and seriously damaging to the Xfinity brand.

I hope management reviews the security footage, investigates the conduct of the employees involved, and publicly explains whether customers are supposed to be treated this way.

one_star_reviews.text: I've watched this place go from 4.5-5 stars when it opened up to 3.5 stars on yelp. Yesterday is going to be my last time going to eat at this place. Primarily due to the service and the lack of attention you get from the staff. I am vegetarian, and when I first went to Papa Zhang's a few months ago, I always ask them in case that if their vegetarian options are made of chicken broth. They always say no, and they indicated on their menu that the broth options are vegetarian. Only yesterday, when we asked a waitress that had been working there for a long time, that their broth contains chicken flavoring, which would make those vegetarian options non-vegetarian. I couldn't believe it at first, so I had asked the waitress to double check with the kitchen. Not sure if she just didn't want to go back into the kitchen and come back out, but she was adamant about her position and was very impatient. Vegans and vegetarians, be aware that the broth is non-vegetarian according to this waitress, and get the clear broth only, if you choose to eat at this place. Anyways, an hour into our meal, we had asked another question for the waitress, in which her immediate response seemed like another brush off, refusing to verify with the kitchen again. Which really infuriated me about service, there seems to be something wrong with each single staff that works there, as each single time I visit, they seem very non-attentive and you'd need to walk up to them while they're scrolling on their phones to get their attention. So a few months ago, they had included lots of appetizer options, in which they started removing them one by one. They had appetizers sitting in the back in which you can grab yourself, but that's now gone too. Stepping into the restaurant yesterday, the first thing they said to us is that they are on a CASH ONLY or ZELLE basis now, not accepting any credit cards. I've worked in restaurants before, so I know this is a way to avoid taxes on your tips. But seeing that in 2026 is absolutely ridiculous. Just a half a year back, they also had lots of dessert options, but now that's replaced with meat, just sitting out there the whole entire day. Also, no more kids discounts at this place, everybody pays the same AYCE price, whether you're 3 years old or 80. SAD to see a restaurant with potential drop to such a 1-star restaurant. Better off going to Boiling World, who at least remained consistent throughout the years. Or even the dreadful LUXE buffet may be better than here.

I am genuinely shocked and disgusted by the experience I had at this Starbucks. I have been to Starbucks many times, and I understand that mistakes happen, especially when a store is busy. I would never normally leave such a negative review over a forgotten topping or a drink being made incorrectly. However, what happened during this visit went far beyond a simple mistake with my order. The way I was treated was completely unacceptable and incredibly disrespectful.

I ordered a Double-Smoked Bacon, Cheddar & Egg sandwich, and when I received it, it was ice cold. This is a hot breakfast sandwich containing egg, bacon, and cheese, so receiving it cold was immediately disappointing and concerning. I had paid for a properly prepared hot breakfast, not something that felt like it had barely been heated.

Unfortunately, the drinks were no better. I ordered a cold brew that was made incorrectly and was missing the cold foam I had ordered. I also ordered a matcha that was supposed to have caramel toppings and whipped cream, and those were completely missing as well. At this point, multiple parts of my order were wrong.

Again, mistakes happen. If the employees had simply apologized and corrected the order, I would have happily accepted the remade items and gone on with my day. Instead, the situation became significantly worse when I politely brought the problems to their attention.

Rather than listening to me and checking the order, I was told that my drinks were “fine.” I was essentially being argued with about an order that I knew was incorrect because I was the person who ordered and paid for it. The missing ingredients were visibly obvious. There was no reason for an argument. All I was asking for was to receive what I had actually ordered.

What disturbed me the most, however, was the way I was treated personally. I am from England, and during this interaction I felt that employees were making fun of my appearance and my English accent. Whether someone sounds American, English, or comes from anywhere else in the world should have absolutely nothing to do with how they are treated as a customer. I found the behavior humiliating, disrespectful, and completely inappropriate for employees dealing with the public.

When I asked for the incorrectly made drinks to be remade, the drive-thru window was slammed shut in my face. I cannot understand how anyone working in customer service could think that was an acceptable response to a customer simply asking for an incorrect order to be corrected.

Eventually, they agreed to “remake” the drinks. However, when they handed them back to me, they appeared to be the exact same drinks with the exact same problems. The ingredients that were originally missing were still missing. After everything that had already happened, this made the situation feel even more disrespectful, because I had specifically explained what was wrong and what needed to be corrected.

I paid for a specific sandwich and customized drinks. I was not asking for anything for free, nor was I asking for special treatment. I simply expected to receive the products I paid for and to be treated with basic courtesy while asking for mistakes to be corrected.

There is a huge difference between an employee accidentally forgetting cold foam or a topping and employees responding to a legitimate complaint with hostility, dismissing the customer, mocking personal characteristics, slamming the drive-thru window, and then apparently handing back drinks without actually correcting them.

I left this location feeling embarrassed, angry, and extremely disappointed. No customer should be made to feel uncomfortable because of their appearance or accent. Being from England should certainly not make me a target for ridicule while I am simply trying to pick up an order.

I would have been completely satisfied with a simple, “We’re sorry about that, we’ll remake those for you.” Instead, what should have been an easily corrected order turned into one of the worst customer-service experiences I have had.

Absolutely unacceptable experience

Paid for bowling and dinner, but ended up leaving hungry and spending even more elsewhere

We came in with our child and fiancé, paid $80 for a bowling lane for 2 hours, and expected to enjoy a fun family night that included bowling and dinner. Instead, we ended up leaving early despite our game still having over a half hour left, going to BJ’s (great experience and customer service) to eat, and spending almost double what we had planned because we received no service at all during our time here.

When we first arrived, our waitress brought us three waters at 7:30 when our lane time started, but after that we were completely forgotten. About 35 minutes into our bowling time, we still had not been greeted to order food or drinks, even though we saw our waitress repeatedly walking back and forth servicing the same three lanes on the far left servicing the same men over and over. I eventually had to walk up to the bar myself to order drinks because no one had come to our lane.

When I returned, I asked a bussed walking by we could get a waitress and was told, “I’ll go find her.” She later came back and said she couldn’t find her but thought someone else would help us. However, both employees continued taking care of the same lanes and never came over to check on us. Again, asked the lady that helped us check into our bowling lane if we can please get a waitress to put a food order in with. She never came.

I once again had to walk to the bar myself to order more drinks because our child was thirsty and we still had not had anyone come take our order. As I was walking back to our lane with two sodas and a drink in my hands, the same employee that assisted with check us in to bowling asked, “She hasn’t come to take your order?” I said no, and she responded, “Oh, sorry,” before i walked over to our lane.

By that point, we had already been there for an hour and 25 minutes and had received absolutely no service beyond the original waters. Not once, if there was cameras will they see the waitress or waitor make it even close to our lane. Not once did a waitress come to lane 1 to take our order or check if we needed anything.

I spoke with the manager and explained everything because our child’s experience was ruined. We booked two hours to bowl, have fun, and enjoy a family night, but our child was hungry and by the time anyone finally came over, our bowling time was almost over. The manager offered an appetizer or brownie, but at that point it was too late.

This is actually the third time we have had issues receiving any kind of service while booking a bowling lane at this location. I completely understand that busy nights, short staffing, weekends, or holidays can make things difficult, but this was a quiet Wednesday night and the location was not busy. There was no reason we should have been ignored the entire time.

I gave this place the benefit of the doubt the first two times, but after the exact same issue happening repeatedly, I can understand why the reviews for this location are so poor. Spending this much money for a family experience and leaving disappointed every single time is extremely frustrating.

Unfortunately, we have learned our lesson and will not be returning.

HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE. Never again.

This gym seems far more concerned with collecting money and protecting its own interests than actually taking care of its members.

One of the things that makes absolutely no sense to me is their membership pricing. Members are paying different prices and supposedly paying for different membership levels, yet at the end of the day, everyone seems to receive basically the same experience. So where exactly is the exclusivity? Where is the difference in service that justifies charging one member more than another? If you are going to create different membership tiers and charge premium prices, there should be clear and noticeable benefits that come with paying more. Otherwise, what exactly are customers paying extra for?

And lately, members aren’t even receiving the basic amenities properly. The massage chairs don’t work, and I was told they have ONE technician servicing all of their locations. For a company with multiple locations, that is unacceptable. It makes you wonder how they can be so organized when it comes to collecting payments but apparently so understaffed when it comes to maintaining the services people are paying for.

What really made me lose trust in this gym, however, was the way they handle their customers and cancellations. When I tried to cancel, suddenly there was a 30-day notice policy that meant they could continue charging me. That policy was NOT clearly explained to me when I originally signed up. Everything seems easy and convenient when they want your signature and your payment information, but when you want to leave, suddenly there are policies and conditions that result in additional charges. The entire process felt misleading to me.

On top of that, I was paying around $600 A MONTH just for personal training. At that price point, I expected a completely different level of service, professionalism, communication, and consideration. Instead, I was flexible and understanding when THEY needed to change my schedule !!!! even when changes were made the same day !!!! and I accommodated them without making it an issue. But when I needed that same flexibility and consideration in return, suddenly it was a different story.

That is what bothers me the most. They expect customers to respect every payment date, policy, and commitment, but that same level of accountability does not seem to apply to them.

You cannot demand premium payments while providing an average experience. You cannot charge different members different prices and then provide essentially the same service while calling one membership more “exclusive.” And you cannot expect customers to be flexible and understanding with your staff while refusing to extend that same courtesy back to them.

After my experience, I genuinely felt that my value to this business was based more on how much money they could collect from me than on keeping me satisfied as a customer.

If you charge premium prices, PROVIDE PREMIUM SERVICE. Maintain your facilities. Be transparent about your membership differences and cancellation policies BEFORE people sign. And most importantly, treat your paying customers with the same accountability and respect you expect from them.

Terrible, terrible experience. Never again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Interstate Moving Experience

We hired Republic Moving & Storage for our move from San Diego to Las Vegas based in large part on the assurances we received before choosing them. Unfortunately, our actual experience was very different from the level of service that was represented to us.

We paid for our move as agreed, but experienced poor communication, careless handling of our belongings, damage to multiple items, and damage to our Pilates reformer. The loading process did not give us confidence that our belongings were being handled with appropriate care.

One of the most concerning moments occurred during delivery when we were offered belongings that were not ours. That raised serious concerns for us about how customers' property was being tracked and handled.

We also experienced an issue involving an additional shuttle charge of more than $950. Before the move, we were told that a shuttle might be necessary and that the driver would let us know if one was required. No one informed us that a shuttle was going to be used or that we were incurring this additional charge. After we disputed the charge, Republic Moving & Storage did remove the shuttle fee, which we appreciate.

Unfortunately, removing that charge does not change the overall experience we had with the move or the damage to our belongings.

We purchased $50,000 in Maximum Value Protection with a $500 deductible and are pursuing a formal claim for the property damaged during the move. We expect that claim to be handled with the level of professionalism and accountability that should have been present throughout the move.

Moving is stressful enough. When you hire a professional interstate moving company, you should be able to expect careful handling of your belongings, good communication, proper tracking of your property, and transparency when problems arise.

While we appreciate Republic ultimately removing the disputed shuttle fee, the damage, careless handling, lack of communication, and being offered another customer's belongings made this an extremely disappointing experience.

Based on our overall experience, I cannot recommend Republic Moving & Storage.
Price

one_star_reviews.text:
We arrived (admittedly late, around 9:40) after a day in Sequoia and the hostess welcomed us and told us they were serving only fried foods because the grill was closed. We said that was fine, were handed menus, sat down, and ordered a drink.
We were then treated terribly by one of the servers; who told us only when taking our orders the kitchen closed in 5 minutes (too late now, we already ordered! We also weren’t the only people in the restaurant and ordering food) and was subsequently incredibly rude the entire time we remained in the restaurant. There were two other servers who weren’t quite so unpleasant, but we saw them less.
We both ordered chicken tenders, and were brought two (two!) tenders each and told we had to be rung up immediately. The total price for a drink and two (clearly made from frozen) chicken tenders and fries each was $48. Which while not a crazy price normally, especially in California, when coupled with the rudeness, and poor quality and lack of quantity of food, $48 before tip felt incredibly pricey.
My partner and I would have fully understood and left if we had been told they were closing soon; having both previously worked in the service industry we know it can be frustrating when people come in right before close. But we didn’t know and weren’t told Bella’s was closing soon, instead we were welcomed in, handed menus, then made to feel unwanted and served terrible food.
We will most certainly be avoiding this restaurant in future.

It tries to cut out every word it can. It hates words such as "just" and "really." Those words have a place, you know. I am disgusted by all of the AI BS that I have to content with. I am a writer. I choose my style, not the system. This latest repackaging just takes it all way too far. Unfortunately, every other software aid that I know about does the same. Also, the screen display is awful. It has gotten worse over the years. The area where my manuscript shows keeps on shrinking. Now, the space on the left reserved for my words remains half empty all the time. The worst part is she was part of the presentation. Because of the experience, I would never go to this winery again.
We met some nice people and because it was my actual birthday I tried to ignore the horrible service.
Poppin wine tours is definitely not worth the money. There are too many other amazing Temecula winery tours to choose from that are much better than this one.  Poppin tours would definitely be at the bottom of the list for me and would never book with them again.

I  had an extremely disappointing experience with Navigated Stay and would not recommend them.

I hired them because I expected a professional property management company that would improve my bookings and revenue. Instead, my listing performed significantly worse than when I managed it myself. During the peak summer season, I received only one booking, and almost every weekend remained vacant. I ended up losing far more in missed rental income than I ever expected.

One of the biggest surprises was discovering that my property was being managed under a host profile with only a 4.6-star rating. In a highly competitive Airbnb market where many successful hosts maintain 4.9+ ratings, I believe this put my listing at a disadvantage. Had I known this in advance, I would have seriously reconsidered signing with them.

To make matters worse, when I wanted to end the agreement due to the poor performance, I was faced with a $2,500 termination fee. Paying thousands of dollars to leave after receiving such poor service made an already frustrating situation even worse.

Overall, I experienced poor communication, disappointing results, and a management service that did not deliver on its promises. I trusted this company with my property during the busiest time of the year, and it ended up costing me a substantial amount of money in both lost bookings and termination fees.

I strongly recommend that property owners carefully review the management agreement, ask which host account will be used for their listing, and compare the company’s actual performance before signing.

Extremely disappointing experience

We were a party of 7 and came to Khazana expecting a good Indian meal, especially given the premium prices. Unfortunately, the entire experience, from the food to the service to the cleanliness, was disappointing.

We ordered 5–6 different appetizers and 4 main courses, so we gave the kitchen plenty of opportunities to impress us. Unfortunately, almost everything was bland and under-seasoned. The food lacked both salt and spice, and at these prices, the taste simply did not come close to justifying what we paid.

The service was arguably even more frustrating. Our waiter seemed completely disengaged and was barely listening to us. Toward the end of the meal, we asked twice for water refills and never received them.

We also ordered a bread basket for the main course. The breads arrived all mixed together, with no explanation of what was what. When we asked the waiter to identify them, his exact response was:

“You guys ordered so much bread that I can't even remember which is which.”

That pretty much summed up the level of service we received.

And then there was the restroom. Stained bathroom, dirty sinks, and generally poor cleanliness. For a restaurant in Palo Alto charging premium prices, this is simply not acceptable.

We were very disappointed with our experience at this club. It often felt like the coach didn’t even want to be at practice, and their lack of engagement showed. Communication throughout the season was poor, and questions or concerns about the team were frequently met with attitude rather than professionalism.

When you’re running a business that works with children and families, respectful communication is essential. The volleyball community is small, and the way players and parents are treated leaves a lasting impression.

Another major concern was the way some coaches treated certain players. They didn’t even seem to try to hide their dislike of certain girls, often showing it through eye rolls, talking down to them, or treating them as though they weren’t worth their time. This behavior was noticed by many parents and players, and it created an unhealthy environment. It was one of the biggest reasons we chose not to return to BRUSA after being there since they opened their doors. If coaches are comfortable treating some players this way, it’s difficult to trust that your own child won’t be treated the same in the future. Parents should be able to entrust their children to adults who genuinely prioritize their well-being, especially when the club claims that mental health is one of its core values.

It also seemed that the club was more focused on competing with neighboring clubs and expanding its influence within local high school programs than on the development, confidence, and mental well-being of the girls entrusted to its care. We expected a positive environment that prioritized both athletic growth and the overall experience of the players, but unfortunately, that was not what we experienced.

UPDATE ********************* 7/28/26*********************

I am extremely disappointed with the way this situation has been handled. My dog, Rocky, suffered a life-threatening emergency, and during one of the most stressful moments of my life, I was told that CareCredit would be 6 months with no interest. When we picked Rocky up after surgery at 5:00 a.m., all of the financing paperwork was completed by the receptionist. I trusted that everything had been processed correctly.

Months later, as I was checking my balance because I expected to be close to paying it off, I discovered that the account had actually been set up as a 36-month reduced APR promotion, not the 6-month no-interest promotion that was explained to me. Because of that mistake, I’ve already been charged over $200 in interest.

I use CareCredit regularly through my own job, so I know that if the wrong promotion was selected, the merchant can work with CareCredit to request a correction. Instead of taking ownership and trying to fix what appears to have been their mistake, I’ve been met with little urgency. When I spoke with Robin at the Elk Grove location, I asked for a call back from someone who could help, but was simply told she didn’t know when anyone would get back to me.

Why would anyone knowingly choose a 36-month interest-bearing promotion when they were told they qualified for 6 months with no interest? I was never informed there were different financing options. I relied on the staff to process everything correctly while I was focused on Rocky’s condition.

Mistakes happen, but what matters is how a business responds. Instead of making things right, I feel like I’m being left to pay for a mistake that wasn’t mine. The lack of accountability has been incredibly disappointing.

If you’re using CareCredit at this clinic, double-check your financing paperwork before you leave. Don’t assume the promotion you requested is the one that was actually applied.

I had been a patient at this clinic for quite some time because of Dr. Singh. He is knowledgeable and helped save two of my molars when I thought they might need to be extracted. I was so satisfied with his care that I regularly drove about an hour and a half from San Jose to Mountain House for my appointments.

Unfortunately, my most recent visit was very disappointing. I went in for a wisdom tooth extraction and placement of a permanent crown. During the extraction, there appeared to be an issue with the equipment that normally sprays water while drilling, so the team had to use an alternative approach. The extraction became complicated, another dentist had to step in, and my wisdom tooth was eventually removed in several pieces. During the procedure, the dental instruments also pressed against my lips, causing painful sores that lasted for several days.

After the extraction, I experienced significant bleeding once I got home. Because my appointment was on a Friday, I tried to contact the clinic over the weekend, but there was no way to reach anyone for guidance. The stitches came out on their own after about five days, and although the pain and bleeding eventually stopped, I was left with an open socket that made me worried about food and bacteria getting into the area while it healed.

During the crown appointment, there was also confusion when flossing, and the wrong tooth was flossed instead of the newly crowned tooth. I was told prescriptions would be sent to my pharmacy, but after nearly two weeks and multiple follow-up calls, my pharmacy still had not received anything. Each time I contacted the clinic, I was told the prescriptions had been sent, but the pharmacy said they never received them.

I truly appreciate Dr. Singh and the care he provided me in the past, but this experience, along with the lack of follow-up and communication, was frustrating and disappointing. I hope the clinic improves its communication, coordination, and quality control so future patients have a better experience.

The Case Manager I saw was unprofessional and a shitty salesman to boot.

I went in one day for a consultation on my neck pain.
On my second appointment, I met with a case manager (Alex) over a video call to go through their findings and a proposed 10-week treatment plan costing $2,700–3,000. They don't take insurance, so this would be fully out of pocket. I've already tried physical therapy, pain management, acupuncture, and massage without success, so I asked some questions: could I do a trial period, or 2–3 sessions, to see whether this approach works for me before committing thousands of dollars?

He kept pushing the full treatment plan, but mentioned  if partway through you decide it's not for you, there's a guarantee where you can stop treatment and receive a pro-rated amount back. When I asked on the specifics of the plan, he got mad and just started with shitty pressure tactics.

Some rough quotes from him:
"I've never even heard that question before. It sounds like this isn't for you. The treatment plan is for people who care about their pain and actually want to treat it. If you don't care about your pain, then it's not for you."
"If you don't think your body is worth investing into, then this might not be for you."
And after I tell him he's right and it's not for me, he closes with a line about how he's sure I'll regret this in 5-10 years when my condition is worse.

????? absolute waste of time and money "consulting" with this guy

To be clear: this review is about that one interaction and the sales approach behind it. It is not a reflection on the doctor I saw or the admin manager, both of whom were genuinely great to deal with. one_star_reviews.text:
I wish I could give 1-800-Pack-Rat zero stars.

This company cost me time, money, and an incredible amount of unnecessary stress.

When I booked my move, I specifically told them I was moving a **4-bedroom house**. Based on that information, they recommended a **16-foot container**. On moving day, it became painfully obvious that it wasn't nearly enough space. When I contacted them about the issue, they completely changed their story and said they meant the container could hold **four bedrooms**. What about the kitchen, living room, dining room, bathrooms, garage, and everything else that comes with moving an entire house? That's not what was represented to me when I booked.

Because I was on a tight moving schedule, I didn't have time to correct their mistake by getting another container. I ultimately had to throw away furniture and belongings because there simply wasn't enough space. This resulted in a significant financial loss that could have been avoided if I had been given accurate information from the beginning.

The customer service experience was just as frustrating. I was transferred to the escalation department **three separate times** and spent over an hour on hold, only to eventually find out that the department wasn't even open. I was later told the wait time for the escalation department was **three hours or more**. When you're in the middle of a move and working against a deadline, that is completely unacceptable.

Then came another headache. I ordered a lock for the container, but **no lock was ever provided**. I later discovered that I had been charged for the lock anyway. When I contacted customer service to have the charge removed, they **again tried to transfer me to the escalation department—even though it was closed.**

I eventually managed to get through to the escalation department. Unfortunately, they had nothing to say about any of my actual concerns and did absolutely nothing to address the container size issue, the misleading information, or the problems I experienced during my move. The only thing they were able to accomplish was refunding the charge for the lock I never received.

The only positive thing I can say is that the driver who delivered the container was friendly, professional, and genuinely helpful. Unfortunately, that one positive interaction couldn't make up for the overall experience.

I've used PODS before, and the difference was night and day. They were responsive, worked with my schedule, and genuinely tried to accommodate me. After this experience, I would choose PODS again without hesitation.

I cannot recommend 1-800-Pack-Rat based on my experience. The combination of misleading information, poor communication, repeated transfers to an escalation department that wasn't even open, and the complete lack of meaningful resolution resulted in unnecessary financial loss, wasted time, and an enormous amount of stress.

one_star_reviews.text: Change extra

1. Internet service: Under CA AB 1414, residents have the right to opt out of landlord-mandated internet. AB 1414 was passed so that tenants can freely explore different internet options without encountering unfair or illegal barriers. You may review official committee/floor reports for AB 1414 in the California State Legislature.

But management blocks all broadband access from existing service providers Smartaira and other ISPs if you opt out. They are doing this to discourage tenants from opting out and skirt the law, so that tenants will have no other choice. You have the right to use broadband internet just like other tenants. At the least, management should permit tenants to get alternate plans directly with Smartaira.

Management contractually mandated internet to residents starting in January 2026 for about 6 months. They told tenants it was mandatory while it wasn’t. After I complained, they changed their website to clarify that the internet is optional.

Tenants who signed leases during this period and were deceived by management would have a viable claim for internet fees paid to the landlord. While the regional manager said they wouldn't stop other ISPs from serving the building, once I had AT&T come in to do a site evaluation, they changed course and stopped AT&T from moving forward. The property general manager also initially misled me by claiming the building cannot support other ISPs. This is incorrect, as the building already has an AT&T fiber line, but they just needed to set up the network inside the building. Management has failed to provide a convincing argument for refusing AT&T to proceed. AT&T has confirmed it can provide services to residents. And I believe it can be done without causing material disruption to the building or residents.

Landlord actions have breached the warranty of quiet enjoyment, and I believe the actions violate other laws. Tenants who think this is illegal should get legal advice and contact local and state government agencies and FCC to report management actions.

2. Several legitimate critical reviews were reported and removed by management. An unusual number of reviews and patterns suggest review canvassing and manipulation by Hartwood. They keep reporting my review and taking it down, forcing me to repost it. They care a lot about their image; you will see them replying intensely on Google Maps. In reality, if you are experiencing problems, don’t expect the same response or treatment.

3. Ants are an issue in the building.

4. Access issues via the primary entrance. Delivery drivers, guests, and essential services cannot use the main entrance because the elevator requires a key. The front desk is supposed to buzz them in, but they do not operate 24/7 and are away from the desk many times during business hours. As a result, large number of your doorstep deliveries of groceries, food etc.. will fail. If you live in Building two, be prepared for a long walk each time this happens. Restricting use of the primary entrance with the nearest parking area raises accessibility issues and can interfere with reasonable access and enjoyment of your unit.

5. Package room. All packages are placed in one room that is supposedly organized, but be prepared to spend 5 to 15 minutes searching for your items. Some packages eventually turn up after 2 to 3 days. Others require search and rescue party. The package room setup is one of the worst I have seen. It is unclear how residents here tolerate it.

I relied on the information and service this store provided when I decided to spend my money on this bike. Had I been given more realistic information about the range and performance, I would not have purchased it.

I went to a bike store expecting knowledgeable advice and professional service. Instead, I ended up with a bike that does not suit the purpose I bought it for, along with repeated issues that have required me to keep returning to the store.

If anyone else has experienced similar problems with a bike purchased or serviced at this store, please contact me and share your experience. I am considering pursuing this matter in small claims court and would like to hear from other customers who have had similar experiences.

Based on my experience, I strongly recommend doing your own research and getting any claims about range, performance, repairs, or suitability in writing before purchasing from this store.

I had a very disappointing experience here. It felt like the priority was making money rather than helping my pet.

I brought my dog in because the symptoms clearly pointed to a bladder infection. Instead of simply treating the obvious issue, I was encouraged to approve hundreds of dollars in testing, only to be told exactly what I had suspected and sent home with medication. When the problem came back, I returned because my dog was also limping, and I was immediately quoted another very expensive diagnostic test.

What really rubbed me the wrong way was being told, “Dogs are expensive.” Owning a dog isn’t the issue being pressured into what feels like unnecessary testing is. There’s a big difference between paying for quality veterinary care and feeling like every visit turns into another expensive sales pitch.

Because of this experience, I switched to an online veterinarian who focused on addressing the issue without recommending thousands of dollars in additional charges.

I genuinely hope the management reevaluates its approach. Pet owners come in because they’re worried about their animals and trust that recommendations are made based on what’s truly best for their pets, not what generates the biggest bill.

one_star_reviews.text: I spent one year at this school as a student and it was nothing but a total CLOWN SHOW from the education, the management, the facilities, and EVERYTHING in between. This school is effectively a glorified prison from top to bottom. Believe it or not the school does have you wear bright orange or neon long sleeve shirts so they can spot you easily. You need approval from like 3 different people to get time off from the school if you have an appointment, event, or anything really. The retreat center gets free labor from all the students in which the school will label as doing a trade. Such tasks are moving and cleaning beds, Vacuuming, feeding and cleaning up animals feces on the ranch, and many more which I won’t write for the sake of this already long article I’m writing. Your schedule is always changing constantly at the school because of some new BS the executive director wants so don’t expect to have a proper schedule. The school itself doesn’t have much, if any curriculum at all. When it’s actually time for you to learn a trade you just end up watching the instructor find his tools, help him move or hold something, watch all the staff gather around discussing how they can accomplish something within the budget, OH!!! and if you’re lucky you might end up finally getting proper hands on training before inevitably having to do something for the retreat center. Meals were also complete trash for the time I was there. Breakfast was always sausage and eggs, lunch were always these depressing whole wheat flavorless sandwiches, and dinner was actually fairly decent as it would be different every day. However a decent dinner would be offset by 30+ minutes of announcements you would have to sit through every day during the school week. 95% of those announcements ended up just being the sky is blue or some new BS they want to implement. For the weekend GOOD LUCK, most of the time you’ll be feasting on retreat center sandwiches or Costco chicken. As a student it also felt like the school had an unwritten no fun policy, anything we’d find remotely fun or entertaining in the dorms or somewhere on campus staff members would typically shut it down and try to replace it with some mandatory corny activity which they would label as fun. The faith aspect where I would say this school is at its strongest is also lacking heavily. The school has morning prayer, Noon Mass, evening prayer, and a night rosary which are all required, however it severely lacks in actually getting one to truly understand their faith because of a lack of philosophy. All this prayer just ended up feeling empty because the school never taught the students how to properly pray and properly understand scripture. Despite all the prayer I did, when I left the school I believe I didn’t grow in my faith at all despite the amount of prayer we did together. When you try to discuss changing things about the school, PARTICULARLY with the executive director he will just tell you to leave the school and he doesn’t want complainers at his school and things won’t change. I’m really only scratching the surface as there are many other shady and questionable things this school and retreat center implement and expect the students to do. Even If you did manage to complete 2 years at Santiago due to it being unaccredited your career outlook is very bleak along with your training, there is no guarantee for you to get a job outside of the Santiago ecosystem. If you read this far, I’m basically saying STAY AS FAR AWAY AS POSSIBLE FROM THIS SCHOOL!!!!! Don’t even consider this as an option because sitting on your couch doing nothing with a part time job would be better than attending Santiago Catholic Trade School. I truly hope and pray this school can work out and fix all of its major flaws in the future, but I don’t expect that to happen for another 10-15 years.

one_star_reviews.text:
I tried. I really tried to like this dentist because I was so happy to finally have an office close by. Unfortunately, after three visits, the lack of organization, communication, and respect for our time has become too frustrating.

I brought my kids in for routine dental care and wasn’t told beforehand that the first appointment would only be X-rays. I was told the dentist would review them and they would contact me with a treatment plan. A week went by and I heard nothing. I called and was told there was no treatment plan on file for either child and that someone would call me back. No one did.

I called again and was told the same thing. After multiple phone calls, I finally reached someone at the Tesoro office who told me there actually WAS a treatment plan and assured me they would make sure we were taken care of at our next visit.

We arrived and, unfortunately, they were not prepared. They completed one extraction and told us we would need to schedule another appointment for everything else. That’s when I learned they apparently only do ONE item per visit. Two fillings? Two separate visits. Could we at least squeeze the cleaning into one of those appointments? Nope. That needs its own separate visit too.

So if your child needs 2 fillings and a cleaning, you’re looking at THREE separate appointments just to get it all done. And that’s after the initial X-ray appointment so that’s FOUR appointments. As you can imagine, that is a lot of time away from work and school for routine dental care.

Okay… maybe that’s just how they operate. I decided to roll with it.

At the next appointment, we waited about 45 minutes past our scheduled time just for the dentist to see them. Frustrating, but I chalked it up to a busy day and we’re already this far into things.

By the third appointment, we waited 20 minutes in the lobby and then my child sat in the chair for another 40 minutes before anyone even came over. An hour and a half later, all we had accomplished were routine cleanings for both kids.

Unfortunately, I just can’t continue doing this. Between the repeated phone calls, lack of communication, needing a separate appointment for seemingly every individual procedure, and then spending so much time waiting once we actually get there, it has become way too much.

I really wanted this office to work for our family because of the convenient location, and I gave it several chances hoping things would improve. Unfortunately, we’ll be finding another dentist.

My experience with Rula was deeply disappointing, both administratively and clinically. The administrative process was disorganized and required excessive follow-up, adding unnecessary frustration to an already difficult process of seeking mental health care.

The provider experience was particularly concerning. I had already spent hours completing Rula's comprehensive intake questionnaire and submitted the information prior to my appointment, yet the final 20 minutes of my new-patient intake were spent re-collecting information I had already provided. Trauma-related questions were among the final questions, and I was told to focus on "only the factual" rather than the emotional. I became increasingly activated and distressed, yet the appointment ended abruptly with a simple "See you next week." There was no acknowledgment of my distress, no attempt to help me feel grounded, and no meaningful closing conversation. I was left to manage the aftermath on my own.

The provider repeatedly described herself as "tough," but what I experienced was not therapeutic toughness or appropriate directness. I experienced it as emotional detachment and a lack of attunement to the impact of her approach. This was the first appointment I have ever left feeling clearly distressed, activated, and unsafe.

I understand that intakes require gathering information and that providers have time constraints, but I expected a mental health provider to recognize and respond appropriately when a patient is clearly distressed. The combination of poor administrative support and a provider interaction that left me profoundly unsupported has made me question the quality of care Rula provides. I would not recommend Rula based on my experience.
